subject: Helix Labs — cluster connectivity, storage & acceptance next steps
messages:
From: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@helixlabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Helix: cluster sizing & network diagram for private deployment

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for taking this on. Attached are our site inventory and the first-pass network diagram (helix-inventory-20261101.csv, helix-net-diagram-v1.png). We're preparing for a private cluster under our VPC and want to validate a few architectural choices before the kickoff call: 

- Expected steady-state QPS for model inferences: ~250 requests/sec, p95 generation latency target 300ms. Burst up to 1k rps for short windows.
- Tenant model: single-tenant instance for Helix production traffic, but we will have multiple teams and a separate test environment.
- Storage needs: short-term KV cache on local node NVMe (for 1–2 hour retention), model shards on network blockstore, and long-term archive to object storage.
- Network: split management plane (10.10.0.0/24) and data plane (10.20.0.0/20). Need guidance on egress controls, SNAT, and flow logs.
- Compliance: encryption-at-rest + HSM-backed keywrap required. Also need SOC2 evidence for retention and audit logs.

Can you confirm whether the proposed CIDR split works with Redwood's routing/failover model? Any immediate red flags on the storage mix? We can be flexible on node counts but want guidance on the right node classes and sizing for an initial sprint-zero deployment.

Appreciate a short checklist we can use to prep our network/security team before the kickoff.

Best,
Tom
Operations Lead — Helix Labs

Attachments: helix-inventory-20261101.csv (text/csv), helix-net-diagram-v1.png (image/png)

Subject: Re: Helix: cluster sizing & network diagram for private deployment

Tom — thanks for the inventory and diagram, received both. Quick read-through and first impressions below; attaching a short preliminary checklist (redwood-prelim-checklist.pdf) that maps to what your network/security team should have ready for Sprint 0.

Summary (short):
- CIDR split looks fine; we'll want explicit NAT gateway requirements and a proposed egress allowlist for three flows (model downloads, telemetry to our control plane, and optional telemetry to your SIEM).
- Storage mix is reasonable: local NVMe for KV cache, network blockstore for model shards, and object store for archive. We'll call out replication and snapshot expectations.
- KMS/HSM: we support a bring-your-own-KMS flow. For Helix's HSM requirement, we'll need the endpoint + certificate details and a validation window during Sprint 0.

Immediate asks (please prepare these before the kickoff):
1) Confirm expected 95th/99th percentile request sizes (tokens) and concurrency per request.
2) Provide IP ranges that will be allowed to reach control-plane APIs and the NAT egress ranges for outbound model pull.
3) Decide if you'd like local NVMe to be ephemeral only or backed up to blockstore on a schedule.
4) If you require host-based disk encryption (LUKS): confirm scope and provide key custody owner.

Recommended initial node profile (baseline for discussion):
- gpu-serve: 6 x A10-class GPUs, 48 vCPU, 384GB RAM, 1 x 4TB NVMe local (for shard prefetch and KV caching)
- control-plane: 3 x 8vCPU, 32GB RAM (dedicated, no GPUs)
- async-workers: 4 x 16vCPU, 64GB RAM (CPU-only for preprocessing/transform)

Next steps: can we schedule a 60-minute technical walk-through with your network+security + our infra engs (Karthik + Monica) tomorrow or Thursday? I can also share a short acceptance-test checklist and a link to our load-testing harness in Confluence.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@helixlabs.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T08:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Helix: cluster sizing & network diagram for private deployment

Tom / team — adding a few technical constraints/recommendations from the runtime/ops side so you have concrete guidance for capacity planning and network configuration.

Storage and node recommendations (details):
- Local NVMe (fast cache): use as ephemeral KV cache with a 1–2 hour TTL. Do NOT rely on NVMe for durable model storage. Configure a cron to flush hot shards back to blockstore if you expect warm persistence.
- Network blockstore (durable): recommend a replicated blockstore cluster (Rook/Ceph or storage array LUNs) with replication factor = 3 and a storage class 'blockstore-ssd-replicated' exposing RWX where needed for model shard lifecycle.
- Backups/Archive: objects to S3-compatible endpoint. Snapshot schedule: hourly delta, daily full index. Retention: 30 days hot, 1 year cold.

Node pool sizing (initial):
- gpu-serve (A10 equivalent): 6 nodes, each with 1xA10, 48 vCPU, 384GB RAM, 4TB NVMe (local, formatted XFS for speed).
- control-plane: 3 nodes (anti-affinity), 8 vCPU / 32GB RAM, tainted so only control-plane pods run there.
- burst-cpu: 2–4 nodes 32vCPU/128GB for batch/eviction workloads.

Networking:
- Use Calico in BGP mode for pod networking; advertise data-plane CIDR to your upstream.
- MTU: confirm whether the site transit uses jumbo frames; we recommend 9000 if possible.
- Egress: plan for SNAT via a dedicated NAT pool; maintain per-service outbound identity via SNAT ranges so logs can be correlated.
- Flow logs: enable at the hypervisor and gateway level; export to your SIEM. We will need rules for port ranges used by the runtime (gRPC 50051, metrics 9090, model fetch 8443).

KMS/HSM options:
- Preferred: Helix-provided HSM reachable from management plane — provide endpoint + client certs.
- Alternate: Redwood-hosted keywrap with signed attestation; requires SLA agreement for key custody.

Acceptance tests we run in sprint-zero (short list):
- Functional: model pull/populate cache, inference at p95 target under synthetic load, KV miss/backfill behavior.
- Networking: fail-over NAT test, BGP route withdrawal, and blackhole detection.
- Security: KMS rotate and decrypt test, audit log tailing and retention check.

I can drop a sample kube-provisioning manifest and a set of storageclass examples into the Confluence page if you'd like.

—Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
